methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Series C → next-stage step-up multiplier (1.7x) to $1.0B total raised proxy.

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.skip_reason: insufficient narrow peer set in Transportation (found 0 same-stage, 0 adjacent-stage, 0 similar-tier; need ≥3)
methods.rationale: 3 same-sector peers exist in Transportation, but none of the narrow filters (same-stage / adjacent-stage / similar-valuation-tier) yielded ≥3 datapoints. Falling back to all-sector median would be misleading.

data.narrative:
Waabi is a Series C autonomous transportation company founded by Raquel Urtasun, operating within a frontier-tech transportation sector represented by 8 private peers including Rivian, The Boring Company, Einride, Slate Auto, and ZeroAvia. No public comparables exist in this narrow stage-and-sector cohort.

The valuation analysis applies stage-progression methodology, the sole applicable triangulation technique given insufficient same-stage or adjacent-stage peer density. Using Waabi's $1.0B total capital raised as a proxy for current valuation, a 1.7x step-up multiplier typical of Series C to subsequent-stage progression yields $1.7B. The peer-median method proved inapplicable: while 3 transportation peers exist sector-wide, none satisfy same-stage, adjacent-stage, or similar-tier filters required to establish a reliable comparable set; inclusion of all-sector medians would introduce undue bias given the specificity of frontier-stage transportation valuations.

The triangulated analysis supports a range of $1.4B to $2.0B, anchored at $1.7B median. Key uncertainties include the validity of total-raised-as-proxy in absence of prior post-money rounds, concentration of evidence in a single method, and sparse peer comparability in an emerging subsector. Refinement would require either adjacent-stage data or transaction multiples from recent Series C closings in autonomous transportation.
